Based on the provided context, here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable code structure in TypeScript:

```yaml
rules:
- id: "vuln-tabby-1c077147"
  pattern: "await $X(...)"
  pattern-not: "await hostVerifiedPromise(...)"
  languages: ["typescript"]
  message: |
    This pattern matches the use of the `await` keyword followed by an expression. This could potentially be a source of a race condition vulnerability if the expression does not guarantee that the host is verified before it is used.

    To fix this, ensure that the host is verified before it is used. This can be done by using the `await hostVerifiedPromise` instead of `await $X`.
  severity: ERROR
  metadata:
    source-url: github.com/Eugeny/tabby/commit/1c077147acd0a6ec9f8ee80d83a3e9688fbb9444
    category: security
    cwe: [362]
    owasp: [A3]
    references: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html
    technology: ["typescript"]
```

This rule will match any occurrence of the `await` keyword followed by an expression, but it will not match the use of `await hostVerifiedPromise`. This is because `hostVerifiedPromise` is the fixed version of the vulnerable code.

The `metadata` section includes information about the CWE (Common Weakness Enumeration) number 362, the OWASP category A3, and a reference to the Session Management Cheat Sheet. It also specifies that the vulnerability is related to the "typescript" technology.

Please note that this is a basic rule and might not cover all possible variations of the vulnerable pattern. You might need to adapt it to match the specific vulnerability in the patch while keeping it general enough to catch variations of the same issue.
